purpose: Authoritative-vendor connected-worker integration delta adding Operations1 Connected Worker Platform at spec-verified only. Reuses the existing REST/OpenAPI path, pins tenant and API version semantics, records effective-role and webhook-origin security boundaries, and keeps Manufacturing WFM read-only. No customer credentials, customer data, write/control calls, webhook registrations, MCP actions, external-request actions or plant-network probes were used.

systems.name: Operations1 Connected Worker Platform
systems.evidenceNote: Operations1 documents a tenant-scoped REST API at api.operations1.app using a technical API user bearer token whose effective privileges come from the technical user's role. Calls require a dated Accept-Version header; the vendor explicitly advises against `latest` in production. Orders and tasks support pageIndex/pageSize paging, updatedAt range filters and stable ordering fields suitable for bounded incremental reads. Current API history also exposes users, groups, roles, qualifications, documents/work instructions, reports and execution data, while the same API includes mutative role/user/task/order/report operations. Operations1 also publishes webhooks and external-request/IoT capabilities, but the public webhook guidance reviewed does not establish a cryptographic sender-authentication contract and includes a Power Automate example configured for an HTTP trigger callable by Anyone. WFM therefore keeps the trusted Operations1 route REST-only until authenticated webhook-origin/replay evidence or a customer-controlled authenticated gateway is proven. No tenant credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Operations1 technical API user with a customer-approved role constrained to the reviewed read resources only; successful bearer authentication alone is not least-privilege proof
bearer token created with an explicit expiry/rotation policy, injected only at the executor boundary and never written to logs or evidence
exact tenantId binding to the approved Operations1 tenant/subdomain; do not allow tenant substitution or cross-tenant reuse of a token
pin a reviewed dated Accept-Version value in production and reject silent use of `latest`; treat version change as compatibility evidence requiring revalidation
GET/read access only for the minimum approved users, groups, roles, qualifications, documents, reports, orders, tasks, classes/characteristics and related files needed for the mapped WFM workflows

deny user/role/qualification mutation, document/report interaction writes, task messaging/mutation, order creation/update, connector execution, webhook administration, MCP/agent actions and external-request/IoT actions in the normal WFM connector

direct webhook ingestion disabled until vendor-supported sender authentication/signature/mTLS/JWT/HMAC or a customer-controlled authenticated gateway plus replay/idempotency and schema-version proof is available
dataAvailableOrExpected: tenant-scoped users, user groups, roles and qualification assignments/qualification catalogue
digital work instructions/documents, nested steps/process steps, language variants, required/granted qualification context and document structure/classification
orders covering production, manufacturing, maintenance or service work with state, assignments, custom order identifiers, class characteristics and updated timestamps
tasks with state, priority, due/created/updated timestamps, assignments and external classifiers
reports/execution records and exported report data including operator/execution context, order relationships, interactions and outcome evidence where authorised
customer-specific classes/characteristics and external identifiers used to reconcile equipment, locations, orders, products or other local structure
report PDF/media/feedback files only where required by an approved workflow; avoid copying rich media when a compact status/result is sufficient
versioned webhook schemas exist for real-time events, but direct webhook business-data ingestion remains disabled until sender-authentication evidence is proven
automationOpportunities: join Operations1 worker qualifications and role/group context to WFM availability and order/task demand to identify qualified-coverage gaps before they turn into overtime or agency demand
use orders/tasks/reports updatedAt filters with overlap and reconciliation to refresh production/maintenance labour demand without full rescans
compare payable WFM attendance with Operations1 execution/report evidence to identify paid-but-nonproductive or administration time while keeping WFM/payroll authoritative for payable time
detect recurring quality, maintenance or instruction-execution patterns that imply a training/qualification gap and schedule learning before future demand
recommend qualified redeployment between work centres when task/order priority or disruption changes, without mutating Operations1 execution state
poll the authenticated REST API for completion/state changes until webhook sender-authentication and replay controls are proven; only then consider event-driven acceleration

future controlled task/order automation is technically possible, but every Operations1 write remains disabled until a separate authorised write-roundtrip programme proves scope, idempotency, rollback and customer approval
savingsHypotheses: reduce overtime and agency labour by detecting upcoming qualification/coverage gaps from real order/task demand before the shift starts
reduce onboarding and training administration by reconciling qualification and digital-instruction evidence into auditable WFM readiness rather than manually comparing systems
reduce paid idle time and throughput loss by redeploying appropriately qualified workers when tasks, orders or disruption status changes
reduce quality/rework labour by correlating report execution outcomes and recurring exceptions with skill/training gaps
reduce maintenance downtime by combining maintenance/service tasks with real worker availability and qualification readiness

reduce bespoke integration cost by reusing the existing REST adapter, deterministic version pinning and bounded page/updatedAt incremental-read pattern rather than creating an Operations1-specific transport stack
dataGaps: Operations1 is not normally authoritative for employment contracts, absence/leave balances, payable time, payroll rules, agency commercials or complete workforce availability
Operations1 qualification evidence must not automatically be treated as legal/regulatory work eligibility; each qualification source and expiry/competence rule needs an explicit customer mapping

the accessible public documentation confirms 429 responses but does not establish a universal numeric rate limit for all endpoints, so quotas and Retry-After behaviour require authorised-environment evidence

the public webhook material reviewed establishes versioned event schemas but not a cryptographic sender-authentication/signature contract, so direct webhook business-data ingestion cannot yet be trusted
effective read-only role behaviour must be proven in a sandbox/tenant because a technical API user's bearer token can inherit read-only or full-control permissions
offline mobile execution can delay synchronisation; source timestamps and staleness must be preserved so late data cannot masquerade as live workforce state
customer-defined classes, characteristics, external identifiers and group/site structures require versioned customer-specific mappings
multi-site/multi-entity and regional tenant structure must be proven per customer rather than inferred from a single tenantId
constraintsRisks: the same REST API includes mutative user, role, qualification, task, order, document/report and connector operations; GET-only intent does not substitute for effective role proof
bearer tokens can be created with an optional expiry; production WFM must enforce customer-approved expiry/rotation rather than accepting indefinite reusable tokens
the tenantId is part of the request path and must be pinned to the connection identity to prevent cross-tenant substitution
the API requires Accept-Version and the vendor warns that `latest` can fall forward to breaking changes; production connectors must pin a dated version and fail/degrade on unreviewed schema drift
pageIndex/pageSize reads over moving datasets require deterministic ordering, updatedAt overlap, stable-id/digest deduplication and final reconciliation before checkpoints advance
429 is documented but a universal numeric limit is not; use adaptive backoff and provider headers/observed limits rather than a guessed fixed quota

direct webhook ingestion is withheld because current public guidance does not prove sender authentication and demonstrates an Anyone-callable Power Automate receiver; use authenticated polling or a customer-controlled authenticated gateway until stronger evidence exists
Operations1 external-request and IoT patterns can reach external/local infrastructure or devices; the WFM connector must not inherit those outbound automation or plant-control capabilities
Operations1 MCP exposes report search/analytics to AI clients, but the WFM integration plane must not automatically expose bearer tokens or grant MCP/agent action authority

offline/intermittent shop-floor use can produce late or partial state; event/source time, synchronisation time and completeness must be retained and stale data must not silently trigger real-time staffing actions
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI adapter. In an authorised Operations1 sandbox or customer tenant, provision a dedicated technical API user with an explicitly read-only role, pin tenantId and a dated Accept-Version, then prove representative GET reads for users/qualifications, orders, tasks, reports and documents. Validate pageIndex/pageSize pagination, updatedAt overlap/reconciliation, stable-ID deduplication, 429/backoff behaviour, token expiry/rotation, permission denials, custom classes/characteristics, multi-site mappings, offline/late-data semantics and version/schema drift before promotion. Keep webhook ingestion disabled until authenticated sender integrity plus replay/idempotency/schema-version evidence is available; do not invoke MCP, external requests, connector execution, user/role/qualification mutations, order/task/report writes or any plant/device action.
